title: Calculations based on mole concept
notes: **The mole.** One mole contains 6.022 × 10²³ entities (Avogadro's number, Nₐ); the molar mass M in g/mol equals the atomic or molecular mass numerically.
**Mass–moles conversion.** n = m/M; for example 36 g of water (M = 18 g/mol) is 2 mol. One mole of any gas at STP occupies 22.4 L.
**Percentage composition.** The percentage of an element = (mass of the element in one mole of compound ÷ molar mass) × 100.
**Empirical and molecular formula.** The empirical formula gives the simplest atomic ratio and the molecular formula the actual count; molecular mass ÷ empirical formula mass gives the multiplier.
**Limiting reagent and yield.** The limiting reagent governs product mass; percentage yield = (actual yield ÷ theoretical yield) × 100.
